newsitem.title: BELGIUM: South Africa urges EU rethink on trade agreement.
newsitem.headline: South Africa urges EU rethink on trade agreement.

text.p: The head of South Africa's parliamentary trade committee urged the European Union on Tuesday to rethink its stance on liberalising trade with South Africa.
The two hope to sign a wide-ranging bilateral trade and aid pact by the end of this year and the EU has been seeking a deal which would eliminate duties from 90 percent of all bilateral trade.

This excludes the sensitive farming sector, where the EU is seeking duty free access for 90 percent of its exports to South Africa but is only prepared to offer free EU market access to 50 percent of South African farm exports.
Rob Davies said bilateral talks had made progress since this original proposal was made and the EU's negotiating position was now "redundant" and in need of a rethink.

Pretoria had argued that it should be allowed to open up its market more slowly and to a lesser extent than its powerful European partner and the EU had accepted that principle, Davies told a meeting of deputies from the EU and 71 countries in Africa, the Caribbean and the Pacific.
Having accepted this argument in principle, the EU should now accept it in practice in the negotiations, Davies said.
